Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  April 13, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
April 13, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01 p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1 and CS-2.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority, at the
hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/ announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

City/Successor Agency / Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Aisha Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

*Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Warrants and Bills, and problems with the
telephone access code.

Caller (Name Unknown) spoke regarding problems with the telephone access code.
   April 13, 2021

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Padilla that
  the demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  April 9, 2021, in the amount of $4,135,716.61, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 125  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-217 APPROVED – REMY
  MOOSE MANLEY, LLP. Staff report dated April 13, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-217 with Remy
  Moose Manley, LLP (Special Counsel), expanding the scope of services and increasing
  the total compensation from $75,000 to $275,000.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-217;
  and 2) Authorize the payment of Special Counsel’s outstanding invoices ( Attorney-
  Client Privileged ) in an amount not to exceed $91,998.50. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

126  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Faulk that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on August 20, 2020,
  be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None

301  AGREEMENT NO. 21-141 APPROVED – JLEE ENGINEERING, INC.;
  CALIFORNIA CODE SPECIALTIES, INC.; AND THE CODE GROUP, INC. Staff
  report dated April 13, 2021, was presented recommending approval of two-year
  professional services agreements to provide building inspection consulting services for
  the Building Inspection Services Project, per Proposal No. RFP – 0159.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-141 with the following
  consultants: 1) JLee Engineering,Inc.; 2) California Code Specialties, Inc.; and 3) The
  Code Group, Inc., dba VCA Code in an annual amount not to exceed $70,000. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-265 APPROVED – HF&H
  CONSULTANTS, LLC.  Staff report dated April 13, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No.1 to Agreement No. 20-265 with HF&H
  Consultants, LLC broadening the scope of services to include assisting City staff with
  tasks related to integrating Inglewood Municipal Code updates and developing strategies
  for the City's overall compliance with SB 1383.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-265,
  increasing the total contract amount by $25,000 (total contract amount not to exceed
  $268,000). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   April 13, 2021

183  ORDINANCE NO. 21-07 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE FOR THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR
  PROJECT. Staff report dated April 13, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of
  Ordinance No. 21-07 amending Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 2 (Administration),
  Article 5 (Purchasing) by adding Section 2-196.1 ( Inglewood Transit Connector
  Procurements) to authorize the use of alternative project delivery methods and establish
  certain requirements for procurements and contracts related to the proposed Inglewood
  Transit Connector Project ( ITC Project ) initiated pursuant to such authorized alternative
  project delivery methods.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that Ordinance No. 21-07 entitled:

  ORDINANCE 21-07 OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA ADDING SECTION 2-196.1 INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR
  PROCUREMENTS TO ARTICLE 5 OF CHAPTER 2 OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE AUTHORIZING USE OF ALTERNATIVE PROJECT
  DELIVERY METHODS AND ESTABLISHING CERTAIN REQUIREMENTS FOR
  PROCUREMENTS AND CONTRACTS RELATED TO THE PROPOSED
  INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT.

  which was introduced at the meeting held on April 6, 2021, be adopted. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED  SESSION  –  ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION;  WORKERS’
  COMPENSATION CLAIM OF ADRIENNE DODSON: WCAB ADJ NO.
  13059858. Closed session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privilege; City Council
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation Pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(2); Workers’ Compensation Claim of Adrienne Dodson: WCAB ADJ
  No. 13059858.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve settlement in the amount of $58,290. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED  SESSION  –  ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION;  WORKERS’
  COMPENSATION CLAIM OF MARK ROBINSON: WCAB ADJ NO. 12074124.
  Closed session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privilege; City Council Conference with
  Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation Pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(2); Workers’ Compensation Claim of Mark Robinson: WCAB ADJ No.
  12074124.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve settlement in the amount of $60,320. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
   April 13, 2021

127.2  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Mayor Butts:

  EMERGENCY ORDER ADOPTED – IMPOSING A TEMPORARY LIMIT ON
  FEES IMPOSED BY FOOD DELIVERY PLATFORMS. Initiative by Mayor James
  T. Butts, Jr., recommending adoption of an Emergency Order to make it unlawful for any
  food delivery platform to charge a food facility fees totaling more than 15 percent (15%)
  until indoor dining is allowed to resume at 100% capacity.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby Adopt the Emergency Order entitled:

  EMERGENCY ORDER OF THE INGLEWOOD CITY COUNCIL IMPOSING
  A TEMPORARY LIMIT ON FEES IMPOSED BY FOOD DELIVERY
  PLATFORMS TO ARRANGE FOR PICKUP OR DELIVERY OF FOOD
  ORDERS FROM A FOOD FACILITY DURING THE LOCAL EMERGENCY
  DUE TO THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any
  persons present who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with
  City business not elsewhere on the Agenda.

  City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reported an email received from Marvin McCoy, who
  requested his correspondence be submitted as a public comment. She also stated she
  received an email from Susan Janson, who asked for an expansion of operations for
  outdoor pools.

  Stanley Jackson, President of Consolidated Board of Realtors, thanked the Council for
  the opportunity to speak at the meeting. He also spoke concerning a food giveaway on
  April 14, 2021, in celebration of realtors nationwide.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the April 13, 2021, Special Meeting that wasn’t
  held yet.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. 2, 4,
  and 5.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the memory of Joe Bullock, neighbor of Council Member Padilla at the hour
  of 2:15 p.m.

  Approved this 17th day of April, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
